correctness.rationale: For a fixed smooth hard trial with a simple boundary zero, \(\widehat u(y,d)=a(y)d+O(d^2)\) with \(a(y)>0\), while \(\Delta\widehat u=O(1)\). Hence the singular source dominates and \(R\sim-a(y)^{-\alpha}d^{-\alpha}\). Multiplying \(R^2\) by \(1+\beta\widehat u^{-p}\) gives \(d^{-(2\alpha+p)}\), and a codimension-one collar is integrable exactly when \(2\alpha+p<1\). The one-dimensional grid laws are the standard harmonic-sum asymptotics, and differentiating \(d^{2-\alpha}\) verifies the proposed leading boundary correction.
